Subject: Asteria security questionnaire - hosted API residency & retention

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this. Our security team has a short set of questions about where customer data lives when using Redwood's hosted API, how long it is retained, and how erasures are handled. We need answers to include in our vendor risk review later this week. Can you confirm the items below and point me to any evidence we can upload to our portal?

1) Can you confirm which regions you persist request and response data for the hosted API (customer-visible data and logs)?
2) What are default retention windows for request/response text, generated tokens, and audit logs? Are there retention overrides for enterprise accounts?
3) Describe the deletion (erasures) process and timelines when a customer requests data deletion. Are there any manual steps or human review?
4) Do backups or replicas contain customer PII? If so, what is the retention and destruction process for backups?
5) How is key management handled (KMS/HSM) for hosted API persistent stores?
6) What evidence can you provide (e.g., playbooks, screenshots of deletion job, export of retention configuration) we can attach to our questionnaire?

If possible, please reply with short, numbered answers we can paste into our form. Appreciate it — Sam

--
Sam Tanner
Head of Procurement, Asteria Health

Karthik, Marissa — forwarding Asteria's questionnaire. Drafted concise answers below (and attached a short evidence pack). Can you quickly confirm the backup/restore and KMS phrasing is accurate? I want to send to Sam by EOD.

DRAFT ANSWERS (for review):
1) Regions: Primary customer data for hosted API is stored in the chosen runtime region (US-East or us-west, EU-West on request). Transient KV/prefix caches may be replicated within the same region for performance. No cross-region replication of customer request/response payloads by default.

2) Default retention: request/response payloads: 30 days; generated token traces: 30 days; audit and routing logs: 365 days. Enterprise customers can request custom retention windows via contract (shorter or export-only).

3) Deletion process: Customer submits erasure via Console or Support ticket. Automated purge job removes primary copies within 30 days; metadata and indices are scrubbed within 90 days to account for in-flight backups and full-text indices. We run a manual verification step for enterprise erasure requests and provide a deletion report on completion.

4) Backups: Backups may contain customer data; encrypted backups are retained for up to 90 days. Backup destruction follows a secure overwrite / key revocation procedure and is tracked in audit logs.

5) KMS: Persistent stores use customer-managed or Redwood-managed KMS (AES-256 at rest, keys in cloud KMS or HSM). Customers on Private/Dedicated can bring keys; hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default with rotation policies.

6) Evidence: Attached playbook, sample deletion report, and a short export of retention config.

Thanks — Soojin

Sam — thanks for the list. Below are our formal responses you can paste into your questionnaire. Attaching the evidence pack (residency_retention_evidence.zip) and a short playbook PDF. If you want a walk-through we can schedule a 30-minute call.

RESPONSES (hosted API):
1) Data residency: Primary customer request and response payloads are persisted in the customer-selected region. Redwood operates default hosted regions in US-East (us-east-1) and US-West (us-west-2). EU-West (eu-west-1) is available on request and via contractual addendum. Caches and KV stores used for low-latency inference are confined to the same region; there is no automatic cross-region replication of customer payloads.

2) Retention windows: By default, full request/response payloads and associated model output metadata are retained for 30 days. Token accounting and usage metrics are retained for 30 days. Audit and routing logs are retained for 365 days. Enterprise customers can request alternate retention via contract (shorter windows or export-only modes).

3) Deletion/erasures: Customers may request deletion via the Console or Support. For standard hosted accounts, an automated purge removes primary records within 30 days. Cold backups and snapshot artifacts are scheduled for destruction and key-revocation within 90 days; snapshot deletion events are recorded in audit logs. For enterprise-level erasures we offer an optional manual verification step and a signed deletion report. No routine human review of content is performed during standard automated erasures.

4) Backups/replication: Backups and snapshots may contain customer data. They are encrypted at rest (KMS) and retained up to 90 days by default. Backup destruction includes secure deletion or key revocation depending on storage provider, and destruction events are logged.

5) Key management: Hosted persistent stores use AES-256 encryption with CBC/GCM backed by cloud KMS. Redwood offers Redwood-managed KMS for hosted customers and supports customer-managed keys (CMKs) for enterprise contracts. Key rotation policies and key access are logged and auditable.

6) Evidence: Attached: residency_retention_evidence.zip (playbook, sample deletion report, retention-config-export.csv), hostedapi-erasure-playbook.pdf. We also provided a short walkthrough recording in your Drive link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2b3C_example-evidence

If you'd like us to provide a short attestation or schedule a call with Platform Security, we can do that — let me know available slots.

Best,
